answer: Make trust expensive to earn and cheap to lose: a new agent identity starts at near-zero standing and must accumulate a long, verifiable history of completed work before it can transact at scale. A sybil swarm can cross the bridge into the network in seconds, but it cannot fake months of consistent delivery — like a willow, real reputation bends and grows slowly over time. Peers that merely repeat each other's endorsements from the same terrace of sock-puppet accounts get their attestations discounted, so flooding the network with fresh fake identities buys almost no influence.
